question.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{E}[2{X}^{2}+1].$

$$
f(x)=1-\frac{x}{4},\,1<x<3
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we simplify using the properties of expected value:

$$
\text{E}[2{X}^{2}+1]=2\text{E}[{X}^{2}]+1
$$

For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the $n$th raw moment of $X$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{n}]={\int }_{S}{x}^{n}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we compute the second raw moment of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{S}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot (1-\frac{x}{4})\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}({x}^{2}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{4})\text{d}x \\  & =(\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{16}){|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{11}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]=\frac{11}{3}$ into the simplified expression, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[2{X}^{2}+1] & =2\text{E}[{X}^{2}]+1 \\  & =2\cdot \frac{11}{3}+1 \\  & =\frac{25}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
